last-desk.name: The Last Desk
last-desk.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: preview-only high-fidelity visual concept of a mascot-led interactive desktop learning application.
Direction name: The Last Desk.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing. A focused primary screen, one clear primary action, no feature inventory.

USER CORRECTION IS THE MOST IMPORTANT INPUT: Earlier conventional interfaces were rejected as generic dashboards. The user specifically wants an interface that feels like "after class", with an original mascot, beautifully detailed 3D isometric components, and tactile objects you interact with, almost like gamification. Make the PRODUCT SURFACE itself a little after-school world. Do not paste a mascot onto a standard SaaS interface. This should feel collectible, surprising, warm, crafted, adult-playful and memorable, not childish.

Actual inspected visual references attached:
Image 1 / washer-reference.webp: Colorfigures original hand-inked isometric washing machine. Use as visual material guidance: solid colored side faces, slightly imperfect fine ink outlines, very precise seams and mechanical parts, paper ground, bold flat navy cast shadow, muted mint, cobalt, mustard and tomato accents. Do not copy the washer or its branding.
Image 2 / saturday-reference.jpg: Tinycharts "A slow Saturday" isometric scene. Use as composition and mood guidance: miniature inhabited place, warm paper, small meaningful objects, flat shaded architectural solids, annotation labels integrated into the scene. Do not copy that room layout or its people.
Image 3 / tinycharts-reference.png: actual webpage screenshot. Use its paper/ink typography and sense that one can play with a scene, not its grid of thumbnail cards.
These are references for a NEW After Class concept, not edit targets. Do not reproduce the reference webpage, gallery, or skill installation text.

PRODUCT: After Class is a personal YouTube lecture review tool. Capture already happened. The hero use case is explaining what you remember in a Socratic conversation, asking for a hint, inspecting timestamped source evidence if desired, and saving your own learning record. No grades, mastery scores, XP, streaks, gold coins, fake percent complete, leaderboard, idle-game mechanics, provider jargon or invented analytics. Play comes from meaningful tactile actions and companion behavior. Speak and type are supported; recall comes before any answer summary. Do not reveal the answer to the question in this initial review state.

Target Dimensions: 1440 x 1024 desktop web-app content. One flat full-screen application screenshot, no browser/device chrome, no exterior scene beyond the app, no multiple concepts. Current date anchor Tuesday November 3, 2026 America/Los_Angeles; omit visible calendar dates.

VISUAL AND COMPOSITION: very light ivory paper full-page ground, faint restrained isometric drafting grid in scene area only. Small top-left distinctive ink wordmark "After Class" with a tiny original bell icon; top right only "My notebook" and quiet "End review". Main title near upper left in literary serif "The bell rang. Stay curious." and small clear subtitle "A little space to make sense of what you watched." Use warm serif for title and readable sans or mono labels, max 2 fonts. Main scene is a very beautiful miniature LAST DESK IN A CLASSROOM after school, seen at isometric 35-degree angle, filling left 58% of viewport and extending toward center. Not a complete elaborate campus. A pale honey wooden desk on dark green metal legs, one small chair pulled out, short piece of mint chalkboard wall behind it, slant of late-afternoon geometric golden light. Many precise tiny parts: screws, rounded wooden edges, leg joints, pencil groove, little notebook binding. 4-tone solids with fine hand-ink outlines like attached references. Restrained mint, butter yellow, tomato red, cobalt, cream; crisp saturated navy cast shadows. Avoid generic glossy clay/balloon 3D, photorealistic room, plastic shiny stock assets or blur.

MASCOT: an original small eraser companion seated on the desk edge, about 100px high. Chunky warm cream rubber body, coral red eraser cap like a knit cap, expressive two ink dot eyes and tiny blue legs, little paper satchel, shy curious lean toward learner. Tiny dimensional seams and shaded faces, personality from pose. Not an existing mascot or familiar branded character. Its speech slip says "Tell me what stuck." A curious peer, not a grading teacher.

TACTILE FUNCTIONAL OBJECTS: an open notebook on the desk selected as the active review surface; a small cobalt tape recorder at the desk front with large orange record key and physical label "Speak"; a folded lecture reel/file on a hinged source stand at back labeled "Lecture · 06:42", closed so answers aren't exposed; a closed mint journal with a blue elastic band at front labelled "My notes". Use only 3–4 objects, not a cluttered toy inventory. At most two tiny thin leader annotations outside the desk: "Open the lecture" points to the source stand and "Talk it through" points to the recorder. Their purpose is evident.

READABLE WORK AREA: right 42% of viewport, a flat ivory notebook-sheet surface visually connected to the open desk notebook, subtly torn or rounded paper corner, one hairline margin/rule, no nested cards and no chat bubbles. A small stamped label "LOCKS & DEADLOCKS" and smaller "Watched 00:00–12:40". Small "QUESTION 1 OF 3". Main clear tutor question in dark ink around 30px: "Two threads are waiting on each other. How could that happen?" Under it about 200px generous blank ruled-paper response area, faint placeholder "Start with what you remember…" and a small mic control labeled "Speak" along lower edge. Primary cobalt button at bottom "Share my thinking" with a simple send arrow. Below a quiet pencil-icon "A little hint" and tiny "Ctrl Enter". The response area must clearly accept ordinary keyboard typing, not require drawing/dragging. Flat text remains readable; never rotate important text into perspective.
Bottom of app one tiny unobtrusive sentence "Your explanations become your notebook." No progress analytics.

PRIORITIES: functional world, mascot, tactile objects, delightful fine details, generous space, polished typography, one clear action. Use spacing/typography before borders, no dashboard grid, no conventional sidebar, no rows of metric cards, no large empty hero artwork over generic chat underneath. This is a coherent usable active-review interface where physical tools perform the app's real actions.

projection-booth.name: The Projection Booth
projection-booth.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: preview-only high-fidelity desktop app concept for a mascot-led tactile learning experience.
Direction name: The Projection Booth.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing. Design one focused primary screen, not a feature inventory.

HARD USER DIRECTION: The user rejected conventional polished dashboards as generic. They want "After Class" to have a mascot and evoke the feeling of after class; they LOVE 3D isometric interactive components and tools, almost gamified. The environment and machinery ARE the interface. No standard SaaS shell with a cute illustration attached.

Actual reference images attached:
1 Colorfigures washer: reference for original hand-inked isometric solid objects, 4-tone shaded faces, real joints, purposeful switches, mechanical cutaways, sharp cast shadows, restrained colors.
2 Tinycharts Saturday: reference for little inhabited scenes, dimensional spaces, paper-and-ink drafting feel, miniature characters and meaningful state changes.
3 Tinycharts webpage screenshot: reference for illustration craft and hierarchy, not the gallery grid or homepage content.
These are style/composition references for a NEW interface, not edit targets. Do not copy their objects, room layouts, branding or text.

Product truth: After Class is a personal tool for reviewing YouTube lectures you watched. It asks you to explain the ideas, permits speaking and typing, lets you inspect timestamped lecture frames/transcript, and saves a local record distinguishing your explanation from help. Recall first; no recap or answer display before the learner attempts. No XP, streaks, grades, mastery meters, percentages, fake analytics, graph, competitive rewards, model/provider names, or automatic correctness praise. Delight comes from physical controls that map to real actions.
This frame is AFTER the learner's first attempt, and they deliberately opened the source, so a source diagram may now be visible.

Target Dimensions 1440 x 1024, single flat full-viewport desktop app screenshot, no browser chrome, laptop/device bezel, poster border, external mockup background, multi-concept collage or clipped UI. Current date anchor Tuesday November 3 2026 America/Los_Angeles; no visible dates needed.

VISUAL DIRECTION: a cozy little after-hours school projection booth, rich warm charcoal / very dark indigo base, cream paper surfaces, amber lamplight, muted terracotta and dusty cobalt controls. Inspired by the attached inked isometric construction, NOT glossy clay stock icons or photorealistic 3D. Fine expressive black outlines on cream lit parts, precisely shaded volumetric metal and wood, tactile knurled dials and hinges, strong geometric cast shadows. Slightly storybook technical manual, remarkably crafted. Main surface is a scene, not cards in a grid. Max two fonts: literary serif for main question, humanist sans for body/control labels at readable 16px.

COMPOSITION fundamentally different from a side-by-side dashboard: small simple header "After Class" and tiny amber lamp symbol upper left; right "My notebook" and quiet "End review". A low wide stage occupies upper 64% of screen. On LEFT of stage, a detailed original mint-and-cream analog projector at a true isometric angle: two reel wheels, spindle centers, perforated film path, lens ring, metal feet with tiny screws, ribbed vent, amber light beam, a large round blue media dial. Engraved panel "LECTURE" and small digital timestamp "06:42". A physically integrated toggle "Source" is ON, its warm lamp visibly lit; tiny caption "Opened by you". This machine is the source inspector and its dial actually suggests scrubbing lecture evidence; not decoration. Its restrained triangular beam projects to a large cream roll-down screen spanning CENTER and RIGHT. Screen is mostly FRONT-ON for legibility, with dimensional roller, weighted bottom bar, two suspension cords, and very subtle paper texture. On it a compact source diagram of circular wait: "Thread 1" holds "Lock A", "Thread 2" holds "Lock B", simple curved blue arrows labeled "waits for B" / "waits for A". Header "Locks & deadlocks" and tiny source attribution "Lecture frame · 06:42"; keep slide clear and not dense. Small understated link "Open in YouTube ↗" below.

ORIGINAL MASCOT: a little curious cream moth, about 110px tall, with soft geometric folded paper-like wings, amber antenna tips, two ink dot eyes, tiny cobalt cardigan and satchel. Perched on the projector housing with an inviting listening pose, one small wing pointing toward the source dial. It is a study companion who likes lamps, not a teacher or an existing branded character. Speech slip next to it "Let's look closer." Detailed shaded volumetric construction consistent with the scene.

BOTTOM 36% is a WIDE inviting physical school writing ledge continuing across screen; cream desktop with gentle dimensional front edge, not a floating UI card. Main readable text grouped at left 64%: small label "QUESTION 1 OF 3", main question at 27px "What is each thread waiting for?" and below a tiny label "YOUR FIRST THOUGHT" and learner contribution "Each one is holding something the other needs." Above or beside at most one previous conversation snippet, not a dense chat log. To right 36%, generous flat light answer sheet with placeholder "Talk it through, or write here…" and 3-line typing area; integrated "Speak" microphone control at lower left; solid terracotta primary "Share my thinking" at lower right. Small quiet "A little hint" below. Text remains flat, readable and never projected at an extreme angle.

Clear state, one primary action, strong alignment, generous real space. Source controls are spatial tools; the writing ledge stays easy to use via ordinary keyboard or clicks, no forced drag interaction. No sidebar nav, dashboard cards, metrics panels, chat bubbles, chunky rounded app-window panels, neon glow or decorative star confetti. Make a memorable coherent functioning product environment with intimate 'after class' character.

study-bench.name: The Study Bench
study-bench.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: preview-only high-fidelity desktop interface concept for a mascot-led, tactile learning tool.
Direction name: The Study Bench.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing. One focused primary screen, one clear primary action, no feature inventory.

MOST IMPORTANT USER CORRECTION: The earlier conventional interfaces looked like generic dashboards. User wants a mascot, the emotional idea of "after class", 3D isometric components, and tools you can interact with—almost gamified. The physical object must BE the functional interface, not decorative art next to a standard chat app.

Attached ACTUALLY INSPECTED references:
1 washer-reference.webp / Colorfigures: DIRECT and STRONG reference for crisp isometric mechanical objects with solid flat shaded faces, very thin slightly hand-inked outlines, carefully built small details, mint and cream enamel, cobalt geometric cast shadows, warm paper background. This is the closest target for this concept. Avoid imitating the washer object itself.
2 saturday-reference.jpg / Tinycharts: reference for inhabitable miniature spatial scene with small characters, purposeful spatial arrangement and delicate annotations. Do not copy its rooms.
3 tinycharts-reference.png: actual webpage screenshot, reference for paper/ink visual clarity and small annotated playful scenes, not the card grid.
These are references for NEW ORIGINAL UI. Do not reproduce reference branding, gallery, skill install UI, or a washing machine. No faux photograph. No generic clay-rendered blobs. No complex old-time photorealistic room scene.

PRODUCT TRUTH: After Class helps the learner explain watched YouTube lecture material, use source evidence on demand, and save an honest local record. Initial review asks a recall question, never an answer summary. Speak and type are supported. No XP, streaks, scores, mastery, percentages, coins, leaderboards, fake analytics, graph, provider jargon or rewards. Tangible motion should communicate actual app states: listening, reply waiting, evidence open, record saved. All controls must suggest ordinary click/keyboard equivalents. This is a visual proposal, no live functionality claim.

Target dimensions 1440 x 1024 desktop app screenshot filling entire canvas. Flat front-on app viewport, no device, browser chrome, external mockup mat or multiple concepts. Current date Tuesday November 3 2026 America/Los_Angeles; omit dates on UI.

COMPOSITION: airy offwhite warm paper (#f3efdf) whole-page canvas with generous breathing room. Top left small icon of a hand bell and beautiful large "After Class" wordmark in readable serif, under it tiny mono "A workshop for things you’re learning." Top right only text "My notebook" and "End review". Main scene occupies center and lower-left about 72% viewport: a large original tabletop STUDY MACHINE on a small honey-wood bench, true isometric projection with parallel edges, 35-degree downward view, clear strong dimensional side faces and flat navy cast shadow extending down-right. This is a clean OBJECT ON PAPER, like Colorfigures, no enclosed room or full-bleed illustrated scenery.

MACHINE: a highly crafted mint enamel and ivory metal console with about 30 purposeful visible parts: beveled chassis, corner bolts, side vent slots, hinge brackets, rubber feet, brass paper-feed spindle, cobalt handwheel with tick marks, spring-loaded terracotta speak key, small physical microphone grill, source lever and timestamp strip, paper exit tray with binding clips, front label "AFTER CLASS · STUDY MACHINE". Main paper roll feeds upward from machine into a large nearly front-on readable cream question sheet, about 650px wide. Physical housing occupies lower middle, question sheet above it. Text on the sheet stays flat and readable rather than rotated into unreadable perspective. Thin black ink outlines, precise 4-tone shading, no blurry gradients or excessive wear.

Question paper at center-top: tiny stamp "LOCKS & DEADLOCKS", subordinate "Watched 00:00–12:40", label "QUESTION 1 OF 3", big question "Two threads are waiting on each other. How could that happen?" A clean spacious three-line ruled answer area below with placeholder "Start with what you remember…" and small blinking text cursor. The question and answer are the main content; keep text sufficiently large and uncluttered. The answer paper is integrated into the machine, not a generic freestanding app card.
On machine control fascia below paper: a large tactile coral push button with microphone icon and plain label "Speak"; a slim clear state window "Ready when you are"; a large cobalt primary action key labeled "Share my thinking" with a small arrow. Below, a small quiet keyboard equivalent "Ctrl Enter" and hint tab "A little hint". Make the controls read as pressable but comfortable desktop UI. No meaningless gauges or fake status dials.
To machine RIGHT, one slim removable evidence drawer physically connected to the mint chassis, currently CLOSED, with a small paper label "Lecture · 06:42" and handle "Open source". No answer summary exposed. When opened it would show timestamped frame/transcript, conveyed by the obvious drawer control rather than explanatory paragraphs.
A small tray at bottom-left has a single bound paper booklet titled "My learning record", giving a material save metaphor.

ORIGINAL MASCOT: small charming mustard-yellow PENCIL MECHANIC, about 120px high, seated on the machine's upper-left edge. Short hexagonal pencil body with wood graphite tip as small cap, expressive pair of dot eyes, tiny cobalt rolled-up sleeves, little cream shoes, red bookmark scarf. Geometric volume consistent with isometric scene. Curious, industrious adult-playful toy-like friend, not a branded character, not a human teacher. One hand rests on a tiny wrench, the other invitingly points to the blank answer paper. A tiny speech tag says "What’s your hunch?" Only one mascot.
At far right, only TWO small handwritten-style functional annotations using fine hairline leaders, not UI panels: "Revisit the lecture" pointing to source drawer, and "Keep what you worked out" pointing to record tray. Do not invent a right sidebar, chat feed, lesson dashboard, item inventory, metric cards, task lists, or menu list.

TYPE AND FINISH: max two fonts, friendly literary serif for main title/question, crisp modest mono for engraved labels; 16px body baseline, 28–32px question, no text walls. Warm paper, mint enamel, coral button, cobalt primary, deep ink. Minimal tasteful texture on paper only, not grain over all text. No skeuomorphic brown noise. The machine is delightfully precise, explorable, calm and readable at 1440px. Clear visual hierarchy and comfortable spacing before borders; no cards inside cards. A practical original tactile software interface with the specificity and craft of the supplied Colorfigures object.
